title: 6.6 Parametric Equations

icans: I can sketch a curve from parametric equations and show its orientation.
I can write parametric equations for a graph.

vocab: the set of points (x, y) = (f(t), g(t)) for t in an ___________
the ____________ the curve is traced as t increases

blocks.p: Fill in x = t² and y = t/2. Plot the points in order and draw arrows.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Sketching: make a table of t values, plot (x, y) in order of increasing t, and use arrows to show the _______________.

blocks.stem: Sketch x = t², y = t/2 for −2 ≤ t ≤ 2. Show the orientation.

notes: Eliminating the parameter: solve one equation for t and _______________ into the other.

blocks.stem:
Eliminate the parameter.
a.  x = t − 1, y = 2t + 1
b.  x = t², y = t/2

notes: Trig parameters: solve for cos θ and sin θ, then use _______________.

blocks.stem: Eliminate the parameter: x = 3 cos θ, y = 4 sin θ. Identify the curve.
Write parametric equations for y = 1 − x² using (a) t = x and (b) t = 1 − x.
A ball is hit 3 feet above the ground at 88 ft/s at an angle of 35°: x = (88 cos 35°)t, y = 3 + (88 sin 35°)t − 16t². About how far does it travel before hitting the ground?
Eliminate the parameter: x = 2t + 1, y = t − 3.
Eliminate the parameter: x = 2 cos θ, y = 2 sin θ.

tickets.stem: Eliminate the parameter: x = t + 2, y = t².
Eliminate the parameter: x = 5 cos θ, y = 3 sin θ.
Write parametric equations for y = 3x − 1 using t = x.
